text:
devin-runtime: heads up — customer-reported spike in p95 and a bunch of 429s on Dedicated pool 'west-2-shared-99' starting ~10:20UTC. They claim requests are being throttled even though capacity should be fine.

maria-ops: saw alerts too, queue depth jumped from ~200 to 14k. Autoscaler didn't kick until much later. suspect batching starvation + tiny requests.

customer-support: customer says errors like "429 Too Many Requests" and occasional 502 from the edge. They shared sample curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini-open","input":"short prompt"}'
```
They also noted a token billing anomaly where token usage spiked but model output lengths stayed small.

sophie-ml: quick theory: lots of tiny requests producing tiny batches -> continuous-batcher is filling windows but scheduler prefers larger tokens so small requests wait, causing per-tenant queue growth and autoscale threshold based on active tokens not request count. small requests -> high request churn -> KV cache thrash -> lower throughput.

raj-sre: logs from runtime show repeated `BATCH_ERRORED` and `BATCH_TRUNCATED` traces, and OOM evictions on one GPU host that led to degraded batch sizes. paste from nodes: 
```
[2026-09-03T10:20:12Z] node-15 kernel: evicting tensors, free mem now 200MB
[2026-09-03T10:20:13Z] runtime: batch_exec failed: OOM while allocating 1.2GB
[2026-09-03T10:20:14Z] scheduler: queue_depth=14000 active_tokens=42000
```

infra-bot: autoscale event: attempted scale +2 but failed due to instance quota, fallback delayed 4m. Instance quota check shows spikes in other dedicated pools for same region.

maria-ops: actionable repro steps for SRE/Customer: 1) send steady stream of short prompts (~8 tokens) at 120rps from one tenant to reproduce queue growth; 2) set header `x-redwood-tenant: tenant-42` to isolate; 3) enable per-request tracing `X-Trace: 1` — collect `scheduler.trace` and `batcher.metrics`.

devin-runtime: tried repro in staging, saw scheduler favoring microbatches which deferred larger batches; max_batch_tokens config was set to 8192 globally but per-tenant `max_batch_size` was 4, so continuous-batcher created many tiny batches under the max token cap. That mismatch plus throttling policy that counts requests instead of effective tokens caused throttle events.

sophie-ml: mitigation suggestions: - temporarily lower `max_batch_tokens` to 2048 for affected pool so scheduler groups more requests; - increase `max_batch_size` for tenant to 16; - enable `prefill_kv_cache=true` to reduce KV misses; - add per-tenant soft cap to avoid noisy neighbor allocations.

raj-sre: noting auth/billing angle — customer had several failing auth retries earlier (403 -> refresh token attempts) that created a retry storm. support confirmed their token rotation changed and resulted in 401/403 for a subset of requests which retried quickly, inflating request count. ask CS to confirm if they rotated keys at 10:15UTC.

customer-support: confirmed customer rotated keys around 10:16 and their client retried aggressively for ~3m. They lowered retry backoff after we asked and errors dropped, but queue remained high because of scheduling fragmentation.

oncall-bot: created incident INC-2026-4783 and attached heap/profile dumps, scheduler traces, and node logs. paging raj-sre and maria-ops.

maria-ops: short-term fix applied at 10:32UTC: bumped pool throttle limit + reduced `max_batch_tokens` to 2048 for west-2-shared-99, increased `max_batch_size` to 12 for tenant-42. Observed p95 improve from 1.8s -> 430ms over 6m.

devin-runtime: follow-ups: 1) add autoscaler quota guard to fail faster and fallback to nearest region; 2) improve metric that autoscaler uses (switch from active_tokens to weighted active_tokens that penalizes many small requests); 3) add detection for retry storms from auth failures and surface to oncall earlier.

sophie-ml: long-term: consider scheduler policy tweak to prefer consolidating tiny requests into opportunistic batches when KV cache hit rate low. also add a per-tenant noisy-neighbor heuristic that reduces batch weight for tenants over X rps.

raj-sre: I'll coordinate postmortem with CS to confirm billing token spike reconciles (likely from retries). Also will file infra story to raise instance quota for west-2 and add a runbook for token-rotation induced retry storms.

devin-runtime: thanks all. saving traces at https://internal.redwood/trace/1955550000 and attaching to INC-2026-4783. If anyone wants to add short repro scripts I'll commit to `eng-runtime/repros/` folder.
